s0101.literal: He went out as Chancellor of the Marquis of Nanchang but, meeting Hou Jing's rebellion, did not take up the post.
s0101.idiomatic: He was posted as chancellor to the Marquis of Nanchang, but when Hou Jing rebelled he never took up the office.

s0102.literal: When the capital fell, court gentlemen were all seized and bound; someone recommended Huan to the rebel commander Hou Zijian. Zijian ordered his fetters removed, treated him generously, and put him in charge of secretarial records.
s0102.idiomatic: When the capital fell, court gentlemen were seized; someone recommended Huan to the rebel commander Hou Zijian. Zijian had his bonds removed, treated him well, and made him keep the secretarial records.

s0103.literal: At that time Jing's soldiers all indulged their brutal power; Zijian was Jing's trusted inner man, and his commission was weighty. Court gentlemen who saw him all bowed low and bent themselves; Huan alone was proudly at ease and would not submit.
s0103.idiomatic: Jing's soldiers ran riot; Zijian, his trusted confidant, held heavy authority. Every court gentleman who met him bowed and cringed; Huan alone stood proudly at ease and would not yield.

s0104.literal: Someone admonished Huan, saying: "In today's chaotic age, everyone seeks merely to escape with life; the barbarian foe is ignorant—how can one oppose them with righteousness?
s0104.idiomatic: Someone warned Huan: "In this chaotic age everyone only wants to survive; the barbarians know no right—how can you resist them with principle?

s0105.literal: " Huan said: "My life and death are already settled; though I may not yet die, how could I fawn on vicious ugliness to preserve myself?
s0105.idiomatic: " Huan said, "My life is already in fate's hands; though I may not die yet, how could I flatter vicious men to save myself?

s0106.literal: " At that time the rebels plundered children and pressed gentlemen and commoners; Huan each time protected them, and very many were wholly saved.
s0106.idiomatic: " The rebels looted families and pressed the gentry; Huan shielded them again and again, and a great many were saved.

s0107.literal: Soon afterward he suffered his mother's mourning and grieved beyond the rites.
s0107.idiomatic: He soon lost his mother and mourned beyond what the rites allowed.

s0108.literal: At that time all under Heaven was in mourning and chaos, and none could complete the three-year mourning; only Huan and Zhang Zhong of Wu commandery, amid bandit turmoil, upheld the law and were both famed for filial piety.
s0108.idiomatic: The realm was in chaos and almost no one could keep three-year mourning; only Huan and Zhang Zhong of Wu, amid the raids, held to the rites and won a name for filial piety.

s0109.literal: When the Founder served as Chancellor, Huan was made Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education and promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate for Presenting Matters.
s0109.idiomatic: When the Founder was chancellor, Huan became right chief clerk of the minister of education, then attendant gentleman of the Yellow Gate for presenting matters.

s0110.literal: Qi sent Dongfang Lao, Xiao Gui, and others to raid; the army reached Rear Lake, the capital was in uproar, and on all sides communications were cut so grain transport could not continue. The three armies drew supplies only from the capital region; Huan was then made Zhenwei General and Magistrate of Jiankang.
s0110.idiomatic: Qi sent Dongfang Lao, Xiao Gui, and others to invade. Their army reached Rear Lake, the capital was in turmoil, and supplies from every quarter were cut off. The armies fed only from the capital region, so Huan was made zhenwei general and magistrate of Jiankang.

s0111.literal: For years there had been war and famine, households had scattered, and a strong foe had suddenly arrived; levies could be found nowhere. The Founder set a day for decisive battle and ordered Huan to prepare many portions of barley meal wrapped in lotus leaves; within one night he obtained tens of thousands of bundles. The soldiers ate their fill at dawn and threw away the rest; they then joined battle and utterly broke the enemy.
s0111.idiomatic: After years of war and famine the population had scattered and a powerful enemy was at the gates, yet nothing could be levied. The Founder fixed a day for battle and had Huan prepare tens of thousands of barley-ration bundles wrapped in lotus leaves overnight. The troops ate at dawn, threw away the rest, fought, and routed the enemy.

s0112.literal: When the Founder received the Mandate, Huan was moved to Attendant of the Crown Prince.
s0112.idiomatic: When the Founder took the throne, Huan was made attendant of the crown prince.

s0113.literal: In the second year of Yongding he was made Administrator of Jinling.
s0113.idiomatic: In Yongding year 2 (558) he was made administrator of Jinling.

s0114.literal: Jinling from Song and Qi times had been a great commandery; though it had suffered raids, it was still whole and substantial. Former administrators of two thousand dan had mostly practiced oppression and violence; Huan kept himself pure and held to integrity, wife and children all did not go to office with him, and he came to the commandery in a single boat. Whatever salary he received he at once divided to succor orphans and widows; the commandery rejoiced greatly and called him the "Spirit Lord."
s0114.idiomatic: Jinling had been a great commandery since Song and Qi days; though raided, it was still comparatively intact. Earlier administrators had mostly been brutal; Huan lived cleanly, left wife and children at home, and entered the commandery in one small boat. He gave his salary at once to orphans and widows, and the commandery hailed him as the Spirit Lord.

s0115.literal: Yin Qi, a rich man of Qu'e, seeing Huan's dwelling plain and spare, thereupon sent him one suit of clothes and one felt quilt.
s0115.idiomatic: Yin Qi, a wealthy man of Qu'e, saw how plainly Huan lived and sent him a suit of clothes and a felt quilt.

s0116.literal: Huan said: "The Administrator enjoys a fine salary—why could he not provide these himself? But the people are not yet provided for; he cannot enjoy warmth and full belly alone.
s0116.idiomatic: Huan said, "The administrator enjoys a fine salary and could easily afford these himself, but the people are not yet cared for; he cannot keep comfort to himself alone.

s0117.literal: I thank you for your generous intent; please do not trouble yourself further."
s0117.idiomatic: I thank you for your kindness; please give yourself no further trouble."

s0118.literal: Earlier, when Emperor Wen was in Wu, he heard of Huan's good governance; when he ascended the throne he summoned him as Imperial Censor-in-Chief and concurrently Grand Arbiter of Yangzhou.
s0118.idiomatic: Earlier, while Emperor Wen was in Wu, he heard of Huan's good rule; on taking the throne he summoned him as imperial censor-in-chief and grand arbiter of Yangzhou.

s0119.literal: Huan's nature was stern and upright; he was skilled at holding to principle and impeached many; the court greatly respected and feared him.
s0119.idiomatic: Huan was stern and upright, skilled at principle, and impeached many; the court respected and feared him.

s0120.literal: Deeply penetrating the body of governance, whenever he presented memorials the sovereign never failed to praise them; stalled business of the hundred offices was all entrusted to Huan for decision.
s0120.idiomatic: He understood governance deeply; the emperor always praised his memorials, and stalled business of every office was sent to Huan for decision.

s0121.literal: He was moved to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, concurrently Colonel of the Footsoldiers, Secretariat Drafter, in charge of edicts and proclamations, and Grand Arbiter of Yang and East Yang provinces.
s0121.idiomatic: He was made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, colonel of the footsoldiers, secretariat drafter in charge of edicts, and grand arbiter of Yang and East Yang.

s0122.literal: In the fourth year of Tianjia he was again made Imperial Censor-in-Chief; soon he became Minister of the Five Armies, regular attendant and grand arbiter unchanged.
s0122.idiomatic: In Tianjia year 4 (563) he was again imperial censor-in-chief, then minister of the five armies while keeping his attendant and arbiter posts.

s0123.literal: At that time Emperor Wen was unwell; all affairs of the Secretariat were ordered decided jointly by Vice Director Dao Zhongju and Huan.
s0123.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen fell ill, all secretariat business was entrusted to Vice Director Dao Zhongju and Huan together.

s0124.literal: When Emperor Wen's illness grew grave, Huan with Emperor Xuan and Zhongju, together with Minister of Personnel Yuan Shu, Secretariat Drafter Liu Shizhi, and others entered to attend medicine.
s0124.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen grew critically ill, Huan entered with Emperor Xuan, Zhongju, Yuan Shu, minister of personnel, Liu Shizhi, secretariat drafter, and others to tend his medicine.

s0125.literal: Emperor Wen once said to Huan and the rest: "Today the three realms stand like a tripod; the living people are not yet settled; the affairs of the four seas are weighty and require a mature ruler.
s0125.idiomatic: Emperor Wen once told Huan and the others, "The three realms stand divided; the people are not yet at peace; the empire needs a mature ruler.

s0126.literal: I wish, near at hand, to follow Jin's Emperor Cheng, and far off to exalt the law of the Yin dynasty—you must follow this intent.
s0126.idiomatic: I mean, in the near case to follow Jin Emperor Cheng, and in the distant case to exalt Yin succession law—you must heed this intent.

s0127.literal: " Huan then, weeping and sobbing, answered: "Your Majesty's imperial meal is out of harmony; recovery is not far off. The crown prince is in the prime of youth, his sagely virtue daily ascending. The Prince of Ancheng enjoys the honor of a younger brother and is fully fit to be the Duke of Zhou, Yi Yin as assisting minister. If there is any thought of deposing and establishing, your servants in their foolish loyalty dare not hear such an edict.
s0127.idiomatic: " Huan wept as he answered, "Your Majesty's illness is not lasting; recovery is near. The crown prince is young and full of promise. The Prince of Ancheng has a younger brother's standing and could be a Duke of Zhou, an Yi Yin at court. If anyone thinks of deposing and establishing, we in our foolish loyalty dare not hear such an order.

s0128.literal: " Emperor Wen said: "The straight remnant of antiquity—I see it again in you.
s0128.idiomatic: " Emperor Wen said, "The straight remnant of antiquity—I see it again in you.

s0129.literal: " In the first year of Tiankang he was then appointed Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince, the two provinces' grand arbiter unchanged.
s0129.idiomatic: " In Tiankang year 1 (566) he was made grand tutor of the crown prince, retaining his grand arbiter posts in the two provinces.

s0130.literal: When Emperor Wen died, the Deposed Emperor took the throne; Huan was made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Director of the National University.
s0130.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen died and the Deposed Emperor succeeded, Huan was made scattered-cavalry regular attendant and director of the national university.

s0131.literal: In the second year of Guangda he went out as Xinwu General, Chief Clerk to the Southern Central Commander and Marquis of Kangle, Administrator of Xunyang, and acting Governor of Jiangzhou.
s0131.idiomatic: In Guangda year 2 (567) he was sent out as xinwu general, chief clerk to the southern central commander and Marquis of Kangle, administrator of Xunyang, and acting governor of Jiangzhou.

s0132.literal: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, Huan's title was advanced to Renwei General and Chief Clerk to the Cloud-Banner Prince of Shixing; the rest remained as before.
s0132.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, Huan was promoted to renwei general and chief clerk to the cloud-banner Prince of Shixing; the rest of his posts stayed the same.

s0133.literal: Huan in office was pure and sparing; he corrected many things, and Emperor Xuan praised him, bestowing five hundred hu of grain and repeatedly sending edicts with earnest inquiries after his welfare.
s0133.idiomatic: Huan served cleanly and frugally and corrected many abuses; Emperor Xuan praised him, gave five hundred hu of grain, and repeatedly sent edicts of warm inquiry.

s0134.literal: In the third year of Taijian he was summoned as Minister of Revenue and concurrently Right Army General.
s0134.idiomatic: In Taijian year 3 (571) he was recalled as minister of revenue and right army general.

s0135.literal: In the fifth year he was changed to Attendant of the Crown Prince and with Left Vice Director Xu Ling jointly handled the Five Articles of the Masters of Writing.
s0135.idiomatic: In year 5 he was made attendant of the crown prince and with Left Vice Director Xu Ling jointly handled the five articles of the masters of writing.

s0136.literal: In the sixth year he was moved to Minister of Personnel.
s0136.idiomatic: In year 6 he was made minister of personnel.

s0137.literal: In the seventh year he was given the added title Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
s0137.idiomatic: In year 7 he was given the added title scattered-cavalry regular attendant.

s0138.literal: In the eighth year he was changed to Attendant-in-Ordinary.
s0138.idiomatic: In year 8 he was made attendant-in-ordinary.

s0139.literal: At that time there was a northern campaign; Huai and Si were recovered, chieftains of Xu and Yu surrendered in succession, enfeoffments and selections for office piled up in confusion, and Huan met and advanced them—his gate knew no idle guest.
s0139.idiomatic: During the northern campaign, when Huai and Si were recovered and Xu and Yu chiefs surrendered one after another, rewards and appointments piled up; Huan received and advanced them, and his gate never stood empty.

s0140.literal: Moreover he discerned men and was thoroughly versed in the hundred clans; all whom he selected among the gentry in caps and sashes submitted gladly.
s0140.idiomatic: He also judged men well and knew the great families thoroughly; every gentry man he chose submitted gladly.

s0141.literal: By nature he was unyielding and cut off all private requests; though the heir's dignity or the weight of dukes and marquises, if feeling overflowed toward him, in the end he would not bend.
s0141.idiomatic: By nature he was unyielding and refused all private requests; neither the heir's rank nor the weight of dukes and marquises could make him bend.

s0142.literal: When the Prince of Shixing, Shuling, was in Xiangzhou, he repeatedly hinted to the relevant offices and firmly sought capital ministerial posts.
s0142.idiomatic: While Prince Shixing, Shuling, was in Xiangzhou, he repeatedly pressed the offices and demanded capital ministerial posts.

s0143.literal: Huan said: "Capital memorial-review posts are by nature raised through virtue and need not be imperial kin.
s0143.idiomatic: Huan said, "Capital memorial-review posts are raised by virtue and need not go to imperial kin.

s0144.literal: " He thereupon spoke boldly to Emperor Xuan.
s0144.idiomatic: " He then spoke boldly to Emperor Xuan.

s0145.literal: Emperor Xuan said: "How could Shixing suddenly aspire to such a post? Besides, if my son were to hold it, he would have to come after the Prince of Poyang.
s0145.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan said, "How could Shixing suddenly want such a post? Even if my son held it, he would rank after the Prince of Poyang.

s0146.literal: " Huan said: "What your servant sees is also as in the sacred edict.
s0146.idiomatic: " Huan said, "What I see agrees with Your Majesty's intent.

s0147.literal: " Houzhu was then in the Eastern Palace and wished to make Jiang Zong Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince; he had Recorder Lu Yu speak of it to Huan.
s0147.idiomatic: " Houzhu was then in the eastern palace and wanted Jiang Zong as grand tutor; he had recorder Lu Yu raise it with Huan.

s0148.literal: Huan told Yu: "Jiang has the brilliance of Pan Yue and Lu Ji, but not the solid worth of Qiuyuan and Chaofu; to assist and support the heir's palace, I privately find it difficult.
s0148.idiomatic: Huan told Yu, "Jiang has Pan Yue and Lu Ji's brilliance, but not Qiuyuan and Chaofu's solid worth; as tutor to the heir I find it hard to approve.

s0149.literal: " Yu reported it fully to Houzhu; Houzhu deeply resented it and thereupon spoke of it himself to Emperor Xuan.
s0149.idiomatic: " Yu reported this fully to Houzhu, who deeply resented it and then spoke to Emperor Xuan himself.

s0150.literal: Emperor Xuan was about to assent; Huan then memorialized, saying: "Jiang Zong is a man of literary brilliance; the present crown prince already has no little literary brilliance—why rely on Zong!
s0150.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan was about to agree when Huan memorialized: "Jiang Zong is a literary man, but the crown prince already has brilliance enough—why need Zong?

s0151.literal: In your servant's foolish view, I wish to choose a man of solid weight to occupy the post of guidance.
s0151.idiomatic: In my humble view, choose a man of solid weight for the tutor's post.

s0152.literal: " The Emperor said: "If it is as you say, who should hold this?
s0152.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "If that is so, who should hold it?

s0153.literal: " Huan said: "Minister of Justice Wang Kuo, of a family with fine virtue through generations, knowing and by nature solid and quick, can hold it.
s0153.idiomatic: " Huan said, "Wang Kuo, minister of justice, comes from a family of fine virtue and is solid and quick in judgment—he can hold it.

s0154.literal: " Houzhu was then also at the side and said: "Kuo is the son of Wang Tai—he cannot hold the post of Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.
s0154.idiomatic: " Houzhu, who was also present, said, "Kuo is Wang Tai's son—he cannot be grand tutor.

s0155.literal: " Huan again memorialized, saying: "In Liu Song, Fan Chu was the son of Fan Tai and also served as Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince; former ages did not doubt it.
s0155.idiomatic: " Huan memorialized again: "Under Liu Song, Fan Chu, Fan Tai's son, was grand tutor, and earlier ages raised no objection.

s0156.literal: " Houzhu stubbornly disputed it; the Emperor in the end made Zong Grand Tutor, and from this Huan went against the imperial intent.
s0156.idiomatic: " Houzhu argued stubbornly; the emperor finally made Zong grand tutor, and Huan fell foul of the throne.

s0157.literal: His unyielding uprightness was like this.
s0157.idiomatic: His unyielding character was like this.

s0158.literal: His sons were Shaoxin and Shaozhong.
s0158.idiomatic: His sons were Shaoxin and Shaozhong.

s0159.literal: Shaozhong, styled Xiaoyang, also had talent and learning; he reached the posts of Attendant of the Crown Prince and Eastern Staff Officer to the Prince of Poyang, Equal in Rank to the Three Dukes.
s0159.idiomatic: Shaozhong, styled Xiaoyang, was also talented and learned; he rose to crown prince attendant and eastern staff officer to the Prince of Poyang, equal in rank to the three dukes.

s0162.literal: [Uncle] Zuo, Editorial footnote marker 9. was a native of Lanling.

s0163.literal: His great-grandfather Sihua was Song Western Campaigning General, Bearer of the Staff with Equal Court Ceremony to the Three Dukes, and Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Editorial footnote marker 10. enfeoffed as Duke Yangmu.
s0163.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Sihua was Song's western campaigning general, bearer of the staff with equal court ceremony to the three dukes, and right vice director of the masters of writing [10], enfeoffed as Duke Yangmu.

s0164.literal: Editorial footnote marker 11. His grandfather Huilian was Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Director of the Imperial Household Treasury, and Minister of the Left for the People.
s0164.idiomatic: [11] His grandfather Huilian was scattered-cavalry regular attendant, director of the imperial household treasury, and minister of the left for the people.

s0166.literal: Liang Palace Attendant and Minister of Justice.
s0166.idiomatic: Under Liang he was palace attendant and minister of justice.

s0167.literal: Yun was known from youth; his spirit was concentrated and far-reaching, penetrating and with discernment; his bearing was refined and restrained, his movements all fitting rule.
s0167.idiomatic: Yun was known from youth for a spirit concentrated and far-reaching, penetration and discernment, refined bearing, and conduct that always fit the rules.

s0168.literal: He began his career as Legal Clerk to the Prince of Shaoling, moved to Chief Clerk of the Prince of Xiangdong, and was promoted to Attendant of the Crown Prince.
s0168.idiomatic: He began as legal clerk to the Prince of Shaoling, became chief clerk to the Prince of Xiangdong, then crown prince attendant.

s0169.literal: When Hou Jing stormed and took the Terrace City, the hundred officials fled in disorder; Yun alone straightened cap and robes and sat in the palace quarter, and Jing's soldiers respected him and did not press him.
s0169.idiomatic: When Hou Jing took the Terrace City, officials fled in disorder; Yun alone straightened his dress and sat in the palace quarter, and Jing's soldiers respected him and did not molest him.

s0170.literal: Soon afterward he went out to dwell at Jingkou.

s0171.literal: At that time bandits and rebels ran wild, the common people were tossed in waves of terror, and gentry clans fled in all directions; Yun alone did not go.
s0171.idiomatic: Bandits ran wild and the people panicked; gentry families fled in every direction, but Yun would not go.

s0172.literal: When people asked the reason, Yun answered: "The way of life and death has its constant allotment—how can one flee and thereby escape?
s0172.idiomatic: Asked why, Yun answered, "Life and death have their allotted share—how can fleeing bring escape?

s0173.literal: But the birth of hardship all comes from profit; if one does not seek profit, from what does calamity arise?
s0173.idiomatic: Hardship always comes from chasing profit; if you do not seek profit, whence comes disaster?

s0174.literal: Now the common people all wish to bare their arms and dispute great merit; with one word to take minister and chancellor—what business is that of one bookish man?
s0174.idiomatic: Now everyone wants to fight for great merit and win minister or chancellor with a single word—what is that to a bookish man?

s0175.literal: What Zhuang Zhou called fearing one's shadow and fleeing one's footprints—I will not do it.
s0175.idiomatic: What Zhuang Zhou called fearing one's shadow and fleeing one's footprints—I will not do that.

s0176.literal: " He then shut his door and dwelt quietly, eating every other day, and in the end escaped calamity.
s0176.idiomatic: " He shut his door and lived quietly, eating every other day, and in the end escaped harm.

s0177.literal: After Hou Jing was pacified, the Founder garrisoned South Xuzhou and summoned him by letter; Yun again declined on grounds of illness.
s0177.idiomatic: After Hou Jing was pacified, the Founder held South Xuzhou and summoned him by letter; Yun again pleaded illness.

s0178.literal: In the Yongding era, Hou Andu was Inspector of South Xuzhou; he came in person to his hut to express the respect due between elder and younger.
s0178.idiomatic: In the Yongding era Hou Andu, inspector of South Xuzhou, came in person to his hut to pay the respect due between elder and younger.

s0179.literal: In the third year of Tianjia he was summoned as Attendant of the Crown Prince.
s0179.idiomatic: In Tianjia year 3 (562) he was summoned as crown prince attendant.

s0180.literal: Editorial footnote marker 12. In the third year he was made Lingwei General and Assistant to the Administrator of Danyang.
s0180.idiomatic: [12] In the third year he was made lingwei general and assistant to the administrator of Danyang.

s0181.literal: In the fifth year he was concurrently Attendant-in-Ordinary, sent on embassy to Zhou, and on return was made Secretariat Gentleman and Director of the Great Works.
s0181.idiomatic: In year 5 he was concurrently attendant-in-ordinary, sent as envoy to Zhou, and on return made secretariat gentleman and director of the great works.

s0182.literal: In the third year of Zhide he was made Chief Clerk to the Central Guard Prince of Yuzhang, and cumulatively moved to Direct-Communication Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Guangsheng General, Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education, and Interior Steward of the Andre Palace.
s0182.idiomatic: In Zhide year 3 (585) he was chief clerk to the central guard Prince of Yuzhang, then direct-communication regular attendant, guangsheng general, left chief clerk of the minister of education, and interior steward of the Andre Palace.

s0183.literal: When the Garrisoning Prince of Poyang went out to garrison Kuaiji, Yun again served as his chief clerk and concurrently Assistant Administrator of Kuaiji commandery.
s0183.idiomatic: When the garrisoning Prince of Poyang went out to hold Kuaiji, Yun again served as his chief clerk and assistant administrator of Kuaiji.

s0184.literal: Passing the shrine of Lord Ji of Yanling at Yanling, he set offerings of duckweed and water-chestnut, entrusting himself as a friend across different ages, and composed a poem to express his intent—its wording clear and classical.
s0184.idiomatic: Passing Lord Ji of Yanling's shrine at Yanling, he set duckweed and water-chestnut offerings, called himself a friend across ages, and wrote a poem to express it in clear, classical wording.

s0185.literal: Houzhu once asked Cai Zheng: "You and Xiao Yun have known each other for generations—what is this gentleman's resolve and conduct like?
s0185.idiomatic: Houzhu once asked Cai Zheng, "Your family has known Xiao Yun for generations—what is his resolve and conduct like?

s0186.literal: " Zheng said: "In his purity, emptiness, and remoteness he is almost beyond measure; as for his writings, one may speak of them.
s0186.idiomatic: " Zheng said, "In purity and remoteness he is almost beyond measure; as for his writing, one can speak of that.

s0187.literal: " He thereupon recited Yun's poem in reply; Houzhu sighed in admiration a long while.
s0187.idiomatic: " He then recited Yun's poem in answer; Houzhu admired it at length.

s0188.literal: That year he was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Virtue.
s0188.idiomatic: That year he was made grand master of splendid virtue.

s0189.literal: When the Sui army crossed the Yangzi, Yun moved to the Guan region.
s0189.idiomatic: When the Sui army crossed the Yangzi, Yun moved to the Guan region.

s0190.literal: At that time court gentlemen who reached Chang'an were by rule all given office; only Yun and Minister of the Masters of Writing Xie Gang declined on grounds of age and illness. Emperor Wen of Sui approved their conduct and richly bestowed money and silk on them both.
s0190.idiomatic: Court gentlemen who reached Chang'an were usually given office; only Yun and Xie Gang, minister of the masters of writing, declined on grounds of age and illness. Emperor Wen of Sui approved and richly rewarded them both.

s0191.literal: Soon afterward he died of illness in Chang'an, aged eighty-four.
s0191.idiomatic: He soon died of illness in Chang'an, aged eighty-four.

s0196.literal: Editorial footnote marker 13. Upright in conduct with breadth of presence, in bearing he was stern; even in hurried moments he always followed rule.
s0196.idiomatic: [13] Upright in conduct and breadth of bearing, he looked stern; even in haste he kept to rule.

s0197.literal: By nature clever and keen, broadly learned, skilled at literary composition.
s0197.idiomatic: Clever, broadly learned, and skilled at writing.

s0198.literal: He doffed the commoner's garb as Editorial Assistant of Writings and moved to Chief Clerk of the Prince of Xichang, Equal in Rank to the Three Dukes.
s0198.idiomatic: He entered service as editorial assistant of writings, then chief clerk to the Prince of Xichang, equal in rank to the three dukes.

s0199.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion, Emperor Yuan of Liang was Inspector of Jingzhou and many court gentlemen went to join him.
s0199.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion, when Emperor Yuan of Liang was inspector of Jingzhou, many court gentlemen went to him.

s0200.literal: Yin said: "The princes are all contending for power; calamity has only begun. To flee hardship today is not yet the season for choosing a lord.
s0200.idiomatic: Yin said, "The princes are fighting for power; disaster has only begun. To flee today is not yet the time to choose a lord.
